claims.statement: triggerConfigSchema is a JSON blob whose only field is `conditions`; the condition schema (triggerConditionSchema) is a Zod discriminated union over 15 condition shapes: branch, target_branch, label, path_glob, actor, conclusion, check_conclusion, workflow_name, linear_status, sentry_project, sentry_level, jsonpath, text_match, slack_channel, slack_actor.

automationTriggerTypeSchema enumerates the six stored trigger types (schedule, github_event, linear_event, sentry, webhook, slack_event), and TRIGGER_TYPE_TO_SOURCE maps each event-driven type to its AutomationEvent source; schedule is the only type with no event source.

Every AutomationEvent envelope variant (github, linear, sentry, webhook, slack) shares the base fields eventType (dot-delimited), triggerKey (dedup key, atomically enforced by a unique (automation_id, trigger_key) invocation index), concurrencyKey (the scope an event firing blocks on), contextBlock (prompt context prepended at fire time), and meta (logging only, never used for matching).
automationEventSchema is the discriminated union over the five event sources and is the wire protocol validated at the internal normalized-event endpoints before the scheduler sees any event.

conditionRegistry assembles shared label/actor handlers (appliesTo github and linear), a reserved linear_status handler, plus githubConditions, sentryConditions, webhookConditions and slackConditions; every ConditionConfigMap key has a handler, and matchesConditions requires every condition to evaluate true.

Each ConditionHandler declares appliesTo (allowed event sources), validate (run at automation create/update time) and evaluate (run at event-matching time); validateConditions enforces the appliesTo gate at save time and additionally checks GitHub conditions against the selected event type via isGitHubConditionSupported.

check_conclusion and conclusion evaluate identically (both read event.conclusion ?? event.checkConclusion), and getConditionSemanticKey maps check_conclusion to conclusion so dedupeConditionsBySemanticKey prevents storing both for the same semantic meaning.

GitHub conclusion values are event-type scoped: getGitHubConclusionOptions returns CHECK_SUITE_CONCLUSIONS for check_suite.completed, WORKFLOW_RUN_CONCLUSIONS for workflow_run.completed, and an empty list otherwise, so a conclusion condition is only valid on those two event types.

The GitHub event catalog (GITHUB_WEBHOOK_EVENT_CATALOG) is the single source of truth for supported event/action pairs and the conditions each offers: PR events offer branch/target_branch/label/actor, review comments offer branch/target_branch/actor, issue_comment.created offers only actor, check_suite.completed adds conclusion, workflow_run.completed adds workflow_name, and issues events offer label/actor.

path_glob is a parsed-but-unoffered condition: no GitHub webhook payload carries a file list, no normalizer sets changedFiles, and its appliesTo list is empty, so no source can answer it; the handler and schema variant stay so persisted configs still parse.

The webhook jsonpath condition evaluates every filter in the list against event.body via evaluateJsonPathFilter, supporting eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/contains/exists over resolveJsonPath, which walks a literal $.dot.notation path with no array indexing or recursive descent; numeric comparisons return false for non-number values and exists is the only comparison that can pass for an undefined value.

Slack text_match validates and re-verifies at evaluation: patterns are capped at REGEX_PATTERN_MAX_LENGTH (200 chars), regex flags are allowlisted to i and m, the pattern must compile as a RegExp for the regex operator, and the handler validates the untrusted value shape is a non-empty string array before persisting.

The sentry_project condition requires event.sentryProject to be defined, so a sentry_project filter never matches metric alerts (which carry no single project); sentry_level matches any_of against event.sentryLevel.

triggerSources lists the registered trigger source definitions (sentry, webhook, github, slack) that the UI's trigger type selector reads; each TriggerSourceDefinition declares source, stored triggerType, display metadata, eventTypes, and supportedConditions, and linear reserves no source today despite the enum member and shared label/actor/linear_status handlers.

Slack slack_channel conditions are denormalized into automation_slack_channels (SlackChannelStore); the create/update route writes the automation row plus the channel rows (DELETE + re-INSERT OR IGNORE via bindChannelStatements) in one atomic db.batch so the canonical trigger_config and the index cannot drift on a partial failure.

Slack_event triggers require at least one slack_channel condition at create time (validateSlackTriggerConfig), because without explicit channel scoping the engine would otherwise skip condition validation entirely when conditions is empty; the API additionally validates each condition through validateConditions with the trigger source and event type, tagging GitHub conditions the event type cannot answer as event_incompatible.

Scheduler.event selects candidates per source: webhook and sentry events resolve the single automation by event.automationId gated on enabled and not deleted (sentry additionally requires event_type equality); github and linear events join automation_repositories on lowercased (repo_owner, repo_name) with trigger_type and event_type; slack events join the automation_slack_channels index by channelId.

In the scheduler event path, matchesConditions gates starting a new run and startInvocation is called with source event, the event's triggerKey and concurrencyKey; event firings block per concurrency key (never per automation, so unrelated events like PRs 42 and 43 do not serialize), and dedup is enforced atomically by the same unique (automation_id, trigger_key) index used for schedule double-fires.

Slack thread continuity runs before condition evaluation: any reply in a thread with a steerable run (any status, within SLACK_THREAD_CONTINUITY_WINDOW_MS of 7 days, matched by getLatestSteerableRunForThread on the automation + concurrencyKey) is steered into that run's existing session via steerSession and never evaluated as a new trigger; replies outside the window or without a session fall through to re-evaluation.

The scheduler fetches Slack thread history lazily and only once per event (shared across all automations admitted for it) through the slack-bot's /internal/thread-context endpoint with a 10-second timeout, HMAC-signed with the slack-bot's service secret; any failure falls back to the plain ingress context block.

The generic inbound webhook route /webhooks/automation/:id requires Content-Type application/json (415) and Authorization Bearer API key (401), looks up the automation with trigger_type webhook (404 otherwise), verifies the key against the stored SHA-256 hash with timingSafeEqual, caps payloads at 64 KB (Content-Length fast-path plus post-read check), and always normalizes the delivery into a webhook.received event (the webhook normalizer never filters).

Webhook API keys are 32 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues base64url data generated at creation, stored hashed with SHA-256 in trigger_auth_data, shown once at creation, and replaced on regeneration; verification re-hashes and compares timing-safe.

The Sentry route /webhooks/sentry/:id verifies authentication before expensive work: it requires the sentry-hook-signature header and checks the 256 KB payload cap before reading the body, then decrypts the automation's stored client secret (AES-256-GCM via REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and verifies an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body timing-safe; a missing encryption key is 503 and a missing stored secret is 500.

The Sentry normalizer returns skipped with a reason (unsupported_action, unknown_resource, invalid_shape) rather than an event: it rejects sentry-hook-resource values outside issue/event_alert/metric_alert, supports only action created for the modern issue webhook, maps the legacy event_alert regression (action regression or issue.status regressed) to issue.regression with a time-qualified trigger key, and supports only action critical for metric alerts; a skipped normalization resolves to 200 {ok:true, skipped:true} so Sentry has nothing to retry.

The internal normalized-event endpoints /internal/github-event and /internal/slack-event are user-or-service authenticated and additionally gated by requireEventPoster: the principal must be a service and the source's row must name it as the allowed poster (github → github-bot, slack → slack-bot; null rows for linear/sentry/webhook are explicit exemptions for sources that arrive on the control plane's own public webhook surface).

validateAutomationEventEnvelope rejects a body that is not a JSON object, whose source does not match the route's expected source, or that fails automationEventSchema parsing, returning 400 with the offending issue paths and logging automation_event.ingress_rejected; the schema is strip-mode so unknown envelope fields are discarded.

The GitHub internal endpoint piggybacks best-effort PR lifecycle tracking on the same forward: trackPullRequestLifecycle runs in executionCtx.submit, its failures are logged as pull_request_lifecycle.failed and swallowed, so lifecycle processing never affects automation matching.

Forwarding to the scheduler maps reachability failures to 502 ({ok:false, error:'Failed to reach scheduler'}); the slack route is built by the shared createAutomationEventRoute factory while the github route composes the exported steps itself to piggyback PR lifecycle tracking.

For github and slack the bot owns provider ingress (provider signature verification, delivery dedupe, mention suppression, watched-channel pre-filter) and normalizes raw payloads with the shared normalizers; the control plane only authenticates the bot, validates the envelope, and matches. Slack thread history is fetched lazily after admission because the normalizer has no Slack token.

Trigger and concurrency keys encode dedup and concurrency semantics per source: GitHub PRs use pr:<n>:<action>:<sha> dedup scoped to pr:<n>; workflow runs dedupe per attempt (workflow_run:<id>:<attempt>) scoped to the run id; Sentry regressions use a time-qualified sentry_regression:<id>:<lastSeen>; webhook deliveries use webhook:idem:<key> when the body carries an idempotencyKey string else a fresh random webhook:<deliveryId> per delivery so separate deliveries may overlap; Slack uses slack:msg:<channel>:<ts> dedup scoped to the thread (slack:<channel>:<thread_ts ?? ts>).

The Slack normalizer strips the bot-mention token (<@U…> or <@U…|name>), returns null when nothing but the mention remains so a pure mention never fires a channel automation, and caps text at SLACK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH (8 KB).

Context blocks are built per source and treat provider payloads as untrusted: GitHub blocks are wrapped in <user_context> tags with an explicit instruction not to follow contained instructions, webhook blocks warn the payload is untrusted input data and truncate JSON at 4096 chars, Sentry blocks summarize the issue with the top 5 stack frames most-recent-first, and Slack blocks wrap message text in <user_content>.

sig1 per-service auth replaces the shared claimless bearer: each service signs its requests with its own secret, and the signature binds the full request (method, path, canonicalized query, body SHA-256, asserted actor) so a captured credential cannot be replayed against a different request; the control plane holds per-service verification keys (SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_WEB, _SLACK_BOT, _GITHUB_BOT, _LINEAR_BOT).

The sig1 canonical request string is newline-delimited sig1, service, timestamp, nonce, uppercased method, pathname, canonical query, bodySha256Hex, actor; the query is canonicalized by sorting decoded key=value pairs bytewise (UTF-8) and re-encoding, and bodyless requests hash the empty byte string.

The sig1 canonical request layout and canonicalization are pinned by the immutable golden vectors in packages/shared/test-fixtures/service-auth-vectors.json (generated by a retired independent Python implementation); any layout change requires a new format tag (sig2), never an in-place edit.

Service signature verification is ordered cheapest-first: parseServiceSignatureHeader rejects malformed grammar and stale timestamps (outside TOKEN_VALIDITY_MS, 5 minutes) before buffering the body; the body is then buffered with a 16 MB hard cap (SERVICE_REQUEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES) and the HMAC is compared timing-safe against a recomputed signature over the actual request; a missing secret is 500 and unknown services or mismatches are 401.

Actor assertion is namespace-scoped: ASSERTION_RIGHTS maps github-bot to github, slack-bot to slack, linear-bot to linear, and web to null; a service asserting an actor outside its own namespace is rejected 401, and resolved actors become the ResolvedIdentity that identity enforcement derives participant identity from.

Outbound bot → control-plane calls go through signedControlPlaneFetch: signing and sending consume the same method/URL/body values through the CONTROL_PLANE service binding so the bytes sent equal the bytes signed by construction; binary bodies must be serialized before signing, and Content-Type is attached only when a body exists.

Adding a trigger source requires coordinated changes to automationTriggerTypeSchema, the automationEventSchema union, the triggerConditionSchema union, a source module (TriggerSourceDefinition + normalizer + condition handlers) registered in triggerSources and conditionRegistry, and a control-plane candidate-selection branch in Scheduler.event; the scheduler's per-source switch is the control plane's only source-specific matching logic and everything after it is source-agnostic.

The slack-bot polls GET /integration-settings/slack/watched-channels (KV-cached, failing closed to an empty set) to pre-filter channel messages before normalization and forwarding; a watch-list outage pauses slack triggers rather than forwarding every message.
